raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The experimental router (`experimental/sgl-router`) calls each worker's `/server_info` without credentials, from two places: the worker-manager introspection (model ids, PD role) and the `cache_aware_zmq` KV-event discovery. Workers launched with `--api-key` return 401 on `/server_info`, so on a key-protected fleet the workers never join their model pool and the KV-event subscribers are never created; `cache_aware_zmq` silently degrades to min-load.

Inbound proxying is not affected (the client's `authorization` header is forwarded as-is); this is only about the router's own outbound calls.

## Modifications

- New optional `--worker-api-key` flag, stored as `ProxyConfig.worker_api_key` (`Copy` dropped for the `String` field; `Clone` kept).
- `WorkerIntrospector::with_worker_api_key` builds its client with a default `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header (marked sensitive); `run_with_config` selects it when the key is configured, `default()` otherwise.
- The KV-event discovery client built in `main.rs` carries the same default header.
- Proxied client requests are unchanged; per-request `authorization` headers still take precedence over client defaults in reqwest.
- Unit test: `worker_api_key_flag_parses_into_proxy_config`.

Validated against a live five-worker SGLang fleet running with `--api-key`: introspection resolves all workers and all five KV-event subscriptions come up (`kv-events: subscribing` with the right `block_size` and bigram detection); without the flag every `/server_info` call 401s. `cargo test` green (542 passed).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable (router-side config/auth only; no model forward changes).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable (one default header on two internal HTTP clients).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body:
Codex review against current upstream main (2026-07-21): this is the most merge-ready PR in the set. The worker credential is propagated to both introspection and KV-event discovery, startup validation rejects empty/header-unsafe values, and the custom `Debug` implementation avoids leaking the secret. The earlier bot findings appear resolved, while the relevant base tests and lint are green.

An outbound-request assertion proving the `Authorization` header reaches a test server would be useful defense-in-depth, but I do not consider it a merge blocker given the current unit coverage and production validation. From a code perspective this looks ready; the remaining need is a maintainer/CI-label pass.

Codex cleanup follow-up: rechecked all four Gemini findings against `ee27af57b`; each is implemented (redacted `Debug`, startup/header validation, fail-fast client construction, and invalid-key coverage), so I resolved the stale review threads. No code change was needed. Existing lint is green; this remains ready for maintainer review/CI trigger.

CI follow-up: rebuilt on current main as `0afbe2780`. The mandatory-base check, lint, and router formatting are green; all earlier review threads remain resolved and the PR is mergeable. The remaining red jobs are only the missing `run-ci` gate. @slin1237, could you apply `run-ci` and trigger the router tiers when convenient?

Thanks @shanemort1982. Closing this because it has had no updates in 92 days.

Reopen it if the work is still relevant.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a `--worker-api-key` CLI argument and configuration option to authenticate router-originated requests to workers. Feedback focuses on improving security and robustness: specifically, manually implementing `Debug` for `ProxyConfig` to prevent leaking the sensitive API key in logs, validating the API key format at startup to fail fast on invalid inputs, and adding corresponding test coverage.

> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

Done in ee27af5: Config::validate now rejects empty keys and keys that cannot form a valid HTTP header value, so a bad key fails at startup with a clear diagnostic.
Done in ee27af5: with_worker_api_key (and the KV-event discovery client in main.rs) now expect() on header construction. Unreachable after the new startup validation, but loud if ever reached.
